item.title: SolarEdge Says US Home Solar Market Weak Due to Financing Issues
item.description: SolarEdge Technologies CEO Shuki Nir says uncertainty over new tax credit rules for home solar equipment has made it more challenging for providers to raise financing for the systems and has led to softer customer demand for panels.

item.title: Ghana Made $1.9 Billion Loss on Gold Purchases in 2025, IMF Says
item.description: Ghana’s central bank incurred losses of 22 billion cedis ($1.9 billion) in 2025 under a domestic gold purchase program aimed at boosting the country’s foreign-exchange reserves.

item.title: Iran-Linked Cyberattacks on US Water Utilities Continue
item.description: The incidents are expanding and ongoing, according to an information-sharing center.

item.title: Microsoft’s AI Sales Mostly Come From OpenAI, Disclosures Show
item.description: Microsoft Corp. generates most of its artificial intelligence revenue from OpenAI, according to new disclosures from the company.

item.title: Mosaic Phosphate Pains Highlight Hormuz Fertilizer Disruption
item.description: Mosaic Co.’s pullbacks in fertilizer production haven’t been enough to alleviate the impact of surging input costs from the war in Iran.

item.title: Arini, Silver Point Among Lenders Set to Take Over Pfleiderer
item.description: A bondholder group is set to take over Pfleiderer, the struggling wood-paneling company backed by Strategic Value Partners, despite the firm raising fresh debt just eight months ago.

item.title: Ares Eyes $2 Billion Loan Deal in Private Credit’s Slow Year
item.description: Ares Management Corp. is leading a $2.2 billion direct loan to help finance a healthcare services acquisition, in one of the biggest deals since the private credit market was roiled by record redemptions this year.

item.title: BC Partners’ Credit Arm Explores Extending Lifeline to LIV Golf
item.description: BC Partners’ credit arm is leading a group of investors looking at lending money to LIV Golf, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Boeing-Lockheed Rocket Joint Venture Taps Private Bond Market
item.description: Boeing Co. and Lockheed Martin Corp.’s rocket joint venture plans to sell bonds in the private market to refinance debt.

item.title: Canada Billionaire Buys Half of Tech Fund, Commits $125 Million
item.description: A Canadian real estate billionaire acquired half of tech investment firm Vistara Growth, committing as much as $125 million to a new fund in a deal with roots in a business school friendship formed three decades ago.

item.title: Colombia Seizes Explosives Ahead of De la Espriella Inauguration
item.description: Colombian authorities intercepted a bus rigged with explosives in the country’s southwest on Wednesday, underscoring security concerns ahead of President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella’s inauguration.

item.title: Victor Niederhoffer Will Be Missed
item.description: By many friends and speculators.

item.title: Carlyle Says PE Exit Market Open for Sellers of ‘Good Companies’
item.description: Carlyle Group Inc. is seeing a thaw in capital markets that is quickening the tempo of exits from investments across multiple industries, Chief Financial Officer Justin Plouffe said.

item.title: EU Audit Offers Brazil’s Poultry Exports a Path Around Ban
item.description: The European Union will carry out an audit in Brazil at the end of August that could allow the country’s poultry exports to avoid a ban due to take effect on Sept. 3.

item.title: US Diesel Exports Surge to Record as World Grasps for Supply
item.description: The US shipped a record amount of distillate fuel overseas last week as domestic stockpiles fell again, the latest sign that the global scramble for diesel is increasingly draining US supplies.

item.title: Argentina Renews $19 Billion China Swap for Another Five Years
item.description: Argentina secured a key source of reserves through the 2027 presidential election after the central bank renewed its roughly $19 billion currency swap with the People’s Bank of China for five years.

item.title: Google AI Leader Leaves, Hassabis to Be Chair in Seismic Moves
item.description: Alphabet Inc.’s Google is losing some of its most prominent AI veterans in a seismic overhaul that is casting doubt over leadership of a critical area of growth right as competition intensifies. Alphabet shares fell as much as 5.5% on the news.

item.title: Putin’s Push to Cut Rates Piles Pressure on Bank Head Nabiullina
item.description: For years, Vladimir Putin made a point of keeping his distance from Russia’s monetary policy, defending central bank independence, publicly backing Governor Elvira Nabiullina and rarely, if ever, signaling where borrowing costs should go.

item.title: Vanguard Muni Bond Head Paul Malloy Departs Investment Titan
item.description: Paul Malloy, who oversaw roughly $300 billion in municipal assets at investment titan Vanguard Group, has left the firm after over two decades.

item.title: UK’s Bodycote Draws £1.6 Billion Bids From CVC and Veritas
item.description: Bodycote Plc received takeover bids worth around £1.6 billion ($2.2 billion) each from CVC Advisers Ltd. and Veritas Capital, pitting rival private equity firms against one another.

item.title: Norway Urges US to Ease Tariffs on Seafood Industry, Citing Discrimination
item.description: Norway wants the US to rein in tariffs that are hurting its seafood industry compared with rivals from other parts of the world.

item.title: Kashkari Says Fed Should Raise Rates Now to Bring Down Inflation
item.description: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari said the US central bank should start to raise interest rates incrementally right now to curb inflation that remains too high.

item.title: Amazon’s Zoox to Levy Fares, in US First for Controls-Free Taxis
item.description: Amazon.com Inc.’s Zoox robotaxi division will start charging fares next week in Las Vegas, marking a first in the US for autonomous vehicles without driver controls.

item.title: Meta Apologizes to Indian Officials Over Removal of Modi’s Video
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc. apologized to Indian officials for temporarily restricting a Facebook post of Prime Minister Narendra Modi, seeking to assuage the government’s concerns in a key growth market.

item.title: Brazil’s CSN Seeks $2.9 Billion for Sales of Entire Cement Unit
item.description: Benjamin Steinbruch’s Cia. Siderúrgica Nacional is seeking at least 15 billion reais ($2.9 billion) for its cement business and expects to receive four bids as it moves to sell the entire unit, according to a person familiar with the matter.

item.title: US Services Activity Continues to Expand on Resilient Demand
item.description: The US service sector expanded at a steady pace in July, bolstered by a pickup in new orders and business activity.

item.title: Vusion Explores Strategic Options, Including Possible Sale
item.description: Vusion is in the early stages of exploring strategic options, including a potential sale, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: SpaceX’s $101 Billion Unlock Heaps Pressure on Battered Shares
item.description: Investors hanging onto SpaceX shares after a plunge below their IPO price are bracing for the next potential hit, when $101 billion worth of stock becomes available for trading on Thursday.

item.title: Stray Piece of SpaceX Falcon 9 Rocket Slams Into the Moon
item.description: A leftover piece of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket likely slammed into the surface of the moon early Wednesday, about 18 months after being sent into orbit.

item.title: PayPal Puts Revenue Targets on Key Units as CEO Reviews Strategy
item.description: PayPal Holdings Inc.’s new chief executive officer, who’s stayed quiet publicly as potential suitors circle the firm, said he plans for the first time to break out results and assign revenue targets for its three main businesses to give investors a better sense of the units’ potential.
